entities.summary: Fascist architecture encompasses various stylistic trends in architecture developed by architects of fascist states, primarily in the early 20th century. Fascist architectural styles gained popularity in the late 1920s with the rise of modernism along with the ultranationalism associated with fascist governments in western Europe. Fascist styles often resemble that of ancient Rome, but can extend to modern aesthetics as well. Fascist-era buildings are frequently constructed with particular concern given to symmetry, simplicity, and monumental size, especially for public buildings. fascist architecture is a architectural style with roots in Europe.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Fascist architecture had a significant regional impact on European urban planning and monument design during the interwar period, influencing architectural styles in Italy, Germany, and Spain. Many iconic buildings constructed under fascist regimes remain prominent landmarks today.
